title: Popescu's local problem is resolvable in characteristic p for geometrically regular Lambda
statement: Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $A$ a $k$-algebra of finite presentation, $\alpha:A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $k$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, and let $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/k}\Lambda}$ be as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Assume (1) $\Lambda$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and geometrically regular over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]; (2) $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$ (a minimal element of the set of primes of $\Lambda$ containing $\mathfrak h_A$). Then $k\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution].

proof.text: Obtain the standardized polynomial-base eighth-power problem and its local essentially smooth factorization from [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-char-p-preparation]. This provides maps beta and gamma with composite alpha, domination of the extended singular ideal, and exactly the annihilator and strict-standardness hypotheses of the lifting lemma.

If the reduced extended singular ideal is outside the quotient prime, its identity factorization is a resolution. Otherwise factor the local map to the essentially smooth intermediate algebra through a smooth algebra using [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-smooth-factors-through-smooth]. Its singular ideal is the unit ideal: 1 has a smooth principal localization, by smooth composition. Thus this factorization is a local Popescu resolution. Delocalize it using the supplied minimality and dimension zero with [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-height-zero].

The quotient map and prime commute with their canonical quotient maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-lift-solution] with the prepared nonempty parameter family and the reduced resolution. This gives a finitely presented R-algebra B with C to B to Lambda resolving gamma.

Compose A to C to B, restrict both maps to k, and give B its composite k-algebra structure. Finite presentation is transitive. The polynomial base R is smooth over k, so smooth R-principal localizations of B are smooth over k. Taking spans, radicals, ideal images and radicals proves popescuIdeal(b) is contained in popescuIdeal(b.restrictScalars k). Combined with domination and the R-resolution this gives both ideal conditions for the original problem. The factorization equality is checked on each element using the two supplied factorization equalities.
